options.why: States the total distance instead of dividing distance by time.
Divides $180$ by $4$ instead of the actual elapsed time of $2.5\text{ hours}$.
Divides $180$ by $2$ instead of $2.5\text{ hours}$.
Excludes the 0.5 hour rest stop from the total time (calculating $\frac{150}{2.4} = 62.5\text{ km/h}$).
Divides total distance $150$ by $4\text{ hours}$ rather than the actual $3\text{ hours}$.
Divides the remaining $60\text{ km}$ by $1.5\text{ hours}$ instead of using total values.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Total distance} = 90 + 60 = 150\text{ km}$
$\text{Total time} = 1.5 + 0.5 + 1.0 = 3.0\text{ h}$
$\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{150}{3.0}$
$= 50\text{ km/h}$

questions.question_text: A motorist drives $120\text{ km}$ at $60\text{ km/h}$ on the outbound trip, and returns along the same $120\text{ km}$ route at $40\text{ km/h}$. What is the motorist's average speed for the entire round trip?

options.why: Averages the two speeds directly ($\frac{60+40}{2} = 50\text{ km/h}$) instead of dividing total distance by total time.
Calculates an incorrect weighted arithmetic mean of the two speeds.
Calculates one-way distance divided by total time ($\frac{120}{5} = 24\text{ km/h}$).

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Time outbound} = \dfrac{120}{60} = 2\text{ h}$
$\text{Time return} = \dfrac{120}{40} = 3\text{ h}$
$\text{Total time} = 2 + 3 = 5\text{ h}$
$\text{Total distance} = 120 + 120 = 240\text{ km}$
$\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{240}{5}$
$= 48\text{ km/h}$

questions.question_text: A hiker walks $8\text{ km}$ to a viewpoint in $2\text{ hours}$, rests for $1\text{ hour}$, and walks $8\text{ km}$ back in $1\text{ hour}$. What is their average speed for the entire $4\text{-hour}$ outing?

options.why: Confuses average speed with average velocity, using net displacement ($0\text{ km}$) instead of total distance.
Omits the 1 hour rest time from the total time (calculating $\frac{16}{3} \approx 5.33\text{ km/h}$).
Divides one-way distance $8\text{ km}$ by total time $4\text{ hours}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Total distance} = 8 + 8 = 16\text{ km}$
$\text{Total time} = 2 + 1 + 1 = 4\text{ h}$
$\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{16}{4}$
$= 4\text{ km/h}$

questions.question_text: A cyclist starts from rest and travels a distance $d(t) = t^2 + 2t$ metres in $t$ seconds. What is their average speed over the first $4\text{ seconds}$?

options.why: States the total distance $d(4) = 24\text{ m}$ without dividing by the elapsed time of $4\text{ s}$.
Computes the instantaneous speed at $t=4$ ($2t+2 = 10$) instead of the average speed over $[0, 4]$.
Divides total distance by $6$ instead of dividing by the $4\text{-second}$ time interval.

questions.question_text: A courier drives $42\text{ km}$ in $30\text{ minutes}$, spends $15\text{ minutes}$ dropping off a parcel, and then drives $28\text{ km}$ in $15\text{ minutes}$. What is their average speed in $\text{km/h}$ for the whole trip?

options.why: Ignores the $15\text{-minute}$ delivery stop (calculating $70\text{ km} \div 0.75\text{ h} \approx 93.33\text{ km/h}$).
Takes only the initial leg speed of $42\text{ km} \div 0.5\text{ h} = 84\text{ km/h}$.
Divides first leg distance $35\text{ km}$ by total time $1\text{ hour}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Total distance} = 42 + 28 = 70\text{ km}$
$\text{Total time} = 30 + 15 + 15 = 60\text{ min} = 1\text{ h}$
$\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{70}{1}$
$= 70\text{ km/h}$

questions.question_text: A swimmer swims $100\text{ m}$ at a speed of $2\text{ m/s}$ and then swims $100\text{ m}$ back at $1\text{ m/s}$. What is their average speed for the total $200\text{ m}$ swim?

options.why: Takes the simple arithmetic mean of the two speeds ($\frac{2+1}{2} = 1.5\text{ m/s}$) ignoring time spent.
Takes the minimum of the two speeds rather than calculating total distance over total time.
Adds the two speeds together ($2 + 1 = 3\text{ m/s}$) instead of finding average rate.

questions.question_text: A boat travels $30\text{ km}$ upstream in $2\text{ hours}$ and returns $30\text{ km}$ downstream in $1\text{ hour}$. What is the boat's average speed for the $60\text{-km}$ round trip?

options.why: Calculates the simple average of the upstream speed ($15$) and downstream speed ($30$): $\frac{15+30}{2} = 22.5\text{ km/h}$.
Takes only the slower upstream speed instead of total distance over total time.
Takes only the faster downstream speed instead of the overall journey rate.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Total distance} = 30 + 30 = 60\text{ km}$
$\text{Total time} = 2 + 1 = 3\text{ h}$
$\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{60}{3}$
$= 20\text{ km/h}$
